1ea6b941fc.what_happened: Parliament is debating Budget 2027 while trade unions and state workers protest against it. The Opposition, including former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris, says the budget fails to address unemployment, living costs, and welfare. The government defends its budget and claims it rebuilt the economy, but critics warn of slower growth and higher inflation.
details: Government doctors have threatened trade union action over their grievances, and nurses, public sector engineers, teachers, principals, university academics, non-academic workers, and Development Officers are also protesting. The government won elections by promising to grant pay hikes twice a year, and the JVP-led NPP secured nearly four-fifths of the postal votes at the 2024 parliamentary election, compared with 61.56% of the overall vote. Government leaders have boasted of overflowing coffers.

Former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris is among those leading the Opposition's campaign against Budget 2027. Speaking at the People's United Opposition political office on Flower Road, Colombo, on Tuesday, he said the budget lacks a practical programme to address unemployment, rising living costs, and declining welfare. He noted that unemployment among educated youth stood at 43%, with approximately 40,000 graduates unable to find jobs, and that nearly half of those unable to secure employment were compelled to seek jobs overseas, while the departure of doctors created approximately 7,000 vacancies in the medical sector and universities have only 6,000 teachers against a requirement of 12,000.

The Opposition says the government has failed to utilise the funds allocated for development, citing a World Bank report that only 16.4% of capital expenditure allocated in last year's Budget had been utilised by September this year, with pending use by year-end expected to reach only 30% to 40% of the allocation. It argues that employment generation requires capital investment to revitalise the economy, attract foreign direct investment, and generate jobs. Ruling party members, however, describe the budget as a magic wand and say the public must exercise patience.

Prof. Peiris compared economic growth of 5% in 2024 with a slowdown from 5.1% in the second quarter of 2025 to 4.2% in the corresponding period this year. He said inflation had risen from 0.8% to 8.3%, while the dollar had climbed from Rs. 293 to Rs. 337. He added that foreign reserves had risen by US$6 billion under Wickremesinghe, compared with about US$1 billion under the present government, and Cabinet Spokesman Dr Nalinda Jayatissa said Wickremesinghe made 33 foreign trips costing Rs. 1,010 million while President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight foreign trips, with 421 individuals accompanying Wickremesinghe from his visit to the United Kingdom on September 17, 2022, to his tour of India on June 8, 2024.
key_facts: Parliament debates Budget 2027 amid trade union and state worker protests.
Government doctors, nurses, teachers, engineers, and university staff demand relief.
The NPP won nearly four-fifths of postal votes in the 2024 election, compared with 61.56% overall.
Prof. G. L. Peiris says the budget ignores unemployment and living costs.
Educated youth unemployment is 43%, with 40,000 graduates jobless.
Only 16.4% of last year's capital budget was used by September.
Growth fell from 5.1% to 4.2%; inflation rose to 8.3%.

1ea6b941fc.whats_next: Industrial action is likely to snowball, threatening economic and political stability. The government should abandon confrontation and negotiate with the trade unions.
1ea6b941fc.blurb: Doctors, teachers, and engineers protest Budget 2027 as the Opposition attacks the government's economic record.
1ea6b941fc.spoken: Welcome. Parliament is debating Budget 2027 as trade unions and state workers protest. Government doctors have threatened industrial action, and nurses, teachers, engineers, and university staff are also demanding relief. The Opposition says the budget does nothing practical for unemployment, rising living costs, or welfare. Former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris said 43 percent of educated youth are unemployed and about 40,000 graduates cannot find work. The government, however, calls its budget a magic wand and asks the public to be patient. It also claims it inherited a bankrupt economy, though critics point to slower growth, higher inflation, and the dollar climbing from 293 rupees to 337 rupees. A minister revealed that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe made thirty-three foreign trips costing over one billion rupees, while President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent far less on eight trips. It warns unrest could snowball unless the government negotiates with the unions.
1ea6b941fc.subject: Budget 2027

2159f83449.what_happened: Eighteen-year-old Nethya Sampath cleared 2.08 metres to win Sri Lanka's first gold at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, India. He did it in one attempt and had a personal best of 2.13 metres. Dineth Induwara Weeraratna also won gold in the men's 100 metres.
details: Nethya Sampath, an eighteen-year-old high jumper from Maris Stella College Thimbirigaskatuwa, won Sri Lanka's first gold. He did this at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, India, which started on Wednesday.
Nethya cleared 2.08 metres in one attempt, and his personal best is 2.13 metres. India's Binoy and Ambriesh also cleared 2.08 metres but needed more than one attempt.

Dineth Induwara Weeraratna won the men's 100 metres in 10.35 seconds. India's Rushiprasad Desai was second, and Sri Lanka's Saad Jamaldeen was third. Sri Lanka also had a runner-up finish in the 1500 metres.

He cleared 2.08 metres in one attempt.

2159f83449.blurb: Teen Nethya Sampath cleared 2.08 metres to give Sri Lanka its first athletics gold.
2159f83449.spoken: Sri Lanka have started their athletics campaign at the BIMSTEC Under-23 Championships in Bhubaneswar, India. The event began on Wednesday, and eighteen-year-old Nethya Sampath from Maris Stella College Thimbirigaskatuwa gave the team its first gold. He cleared two point oh eight metres in the high jump, and he did it in one attempt. His personal best is two point one three metres. A teammate, Dineth Induwara Weeraratna, also won gold in the men's hundred metres, finishing in ten point three five seconds. India did well on the first day, while Sri Lanka took two golds. The championships bring together more than two hundred athletes from six nations.

959abe17e5.what_happened: The Attorney General’s Department disclosed fresh findings against retired Major General Suresh Sallay over allegations of concealing information and misleading investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks. At Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court, Additional Solicitor General Dileepa Peiris said Sallay and Azad Maulana stayed at the same hotel in Ahungalla on August 15 and 16, 2020, and that Sallay changed his position when questioned about telephone records. The court also heard about a medical report, an alleged informant, and a possible former Deputy Inspector General of Police, and the case was set for January 27, 2027.
details: The Attorney General’s Department disclosed fresh findings in the investigation against former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, retired Major General Suresh Sallay, over allegations of concealing information and misleading investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks. At Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court, Additional Solicitor General Dileepa Peiris said investigations established that Sallay and Azad Maulana, who appeared in a Channel 4 documentary on the Easter attacks, stayed with their families at the same hotel in Ahungalla on August 15 and 16, 2020.

Peiris said Sallay first claimed the encounter was coincidental but later changed his position when questioned about telephone records. The Additional Solicitor General argued the circumstantial evidence lent credibility to certain claims made by Maulana. He also alleged that an informant known as Thambi Anna provided military intelligence with information regarding Zahran Hashim six months before the Easter Sunday attacks, and that the relevant file was concealed with Sallay’s knowledge.

Investigators are also looking into the possible involvement of a former Deputy Inspector General of Police. The court was told that a 31-page report by a five-member specialist medical panel, appointed to examine allegations of torture against Sallay while in detention, had been received. Peiris argued Sallay reported psychological stress but did not disclose physical torture to the medical panel.

Bhanuka Mallawarachchi, appearing for Sallay, disputed the prosecution’s interpretation and said the medical report referred to a degrading physical examination of his client. The defence also pointed out that the medical panel recommended further investigations into alleged mistreatment during detention. Peiris told the court that, in his opinion, sufficient evidence existed against former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to name him as a suspect, but any decision to arrest him rested with investigating officers; after considering submissions from both parties, Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena ordered the case taken up again on January 27, 2027, for a report on the progress of investigations.

Sallay first called the encounter coincidental, then changed his position when telephone records were raised. Peiris also alleged an informant called Thambi Anna gave military intelligence about Zahran Hashim six months before the attacks, and a file was concealed with Sallay’s knowledge. 375c29b99b.what_happened: A fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on the ring road that circles Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people and injuring at least 21. The blaze spread to more than two dozen cars and motorcycles, leaving them charred. The highway has since been cleared and reopened.
details: On Wednesday evening, a fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on the ring road that circles Cairo, in the densely populated Waraq (Warraq) neighbourhood of Giza, part of Greater Cairo and north of the old city centre. Egypt's health ministry said at least 31 people were killed, at least 21 were injured, and more than two dozen cars and motorcycles were left charred. Footage showed flames and black smoke rising into the night sky, rescue workers pulled people from burning cars, and firefighters battled the blaze as hundreds gathered nearby.

State media said the fire began when the tanker overturned and spilled petrol over nearby vehicles. Al-Ahram, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation, reported the tanker belonged to a private contractor and that a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, causing the driver to lose control; it then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire. A witness named Ahmed Sameer, stuck in traffic, said he saw the truck and many cars burning and at least eight bodies removed, calling it a shocking scene.

Nearby hospitals treated patients with burns and smoke inhalation, and the health ministry sent 39 ambulances, posting images of health minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar overseeing treatment at a Cairo hospital. He said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and the death toll was preliminary and could rise, and he later visited the scene and hospitals. President Abdel Fatah al-Sisi sent condolences, the regional public prosecutor launched an investigation and ordered DNA samples from the dead to identify victims, and a bulldozer cleared the wrecks before the ring road reopened, according to state media.

Egypt has a poor road safety record, with speeding, bad roads, lax maintenance and weak enforcement of traffic laws blamed for most crashes, and deadly accidents claim thousands of lives each year. Official figures show nearly 6,000 people died on Egypt's roads last year, a rise of several hundred on the previous year, and in January 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a multicar pileup near the southern province of Beni Suef. Egypt has also seen several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas, run-down infrastructure, slow emergency responses and improvised rescue efforts making them more common.
375c29b99b.why_it_matters: It underscores Egypt's poor road safety record, where nearly 6,000 people died last year, and a pattern of deadly fires worsened by run-down infrastructure and slow emergency response.
key_facts: Fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on Cairo's ring road on Wednesday evening.

375c29b99b.whats_next: Prosecutors are using DNA to identify the dead, and the death toll may rise further as it was only preliminary.
375c29b99b.blurb: A fuel tanker fire on Cairo's ring road killed at least 31 and injured 21, charring cars as investigators probe the cause.
375c29b99b.spoken: A fuel tanker has crashed and burst into flames on the ring road that circles Cairo, and the death toll is heartbreaking. Egypt's health ministry says at least thirty-one people were killed and at least twenty-one injured, with more than two dozen cars and motorcycles left charred. It happened on Wednesday evening in the Waraq neighbourhood of Giza. State media say the tanker overturned and spilled petrol, though one report says a fallen power cable made the driver lose control. The president sent his condolences, and prosecutors are using DNA to identify the dead. The health minister warned the toll could still rise. The road has now been cleared and reopened. Officials say Egypt's roads are dangerous, with nearly six thousand people dying last year alone.
375c29b99b.subject: Cairo tanker fire

34882c6a25.what_happened: Sri Lankan police have recruited 257 Women Police Constables to better protect women and children and increase female representation in the service. The recruits entered Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday (23) to begin about six months of basic training. The course covers law, fitness, firearms, disaster management, public relations, leadership, and personality development.
details: The Island reports that 257 Women Police Constables have been recruited by the police to strengthen protection for women and children and raise female representation in the force. The new recruits were admitted to Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday (23) to begin approximately six months of basic police training.

Training will include both theory and practice, covering law, police duties, physical fitness, disaster management, public relations, leadership and personality development, and firearms training. The senior management of the Police College will closely monitor the health and welfare of the trainees throughout the course.

Each recruit will receive the monthly government salary for a Police Constable starting from the date of admission to the college. Police said the goal is to give greater priority to the safety of women and children and to strengthen counselling services that help prevent crime.
34882c6a25.why_it_matters: It aims to make women and children safer, increase female representation in the police, and improve counselling to prevent crime.
key_facts: Police recruited 257 Women Police Constables in Sri Lanka.

34882c6a25.spoken: Good morning. Sri Lanka's police force has welcomed 257 new women constables. The recruits reported to Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday the twenty third to start about six months of basic training. They will study law, police duties, physical fitness, disaster management, public relations, leadership, and firearms. The college's senior management will keep a close eye on their health and welfare throughout the course. From day one, they will draw the regular monthly salary for a police constable. Police say the move is meant to make women and children safer and to give more women a place in the service. They also hope more female officers will improve counselling and help stop crime before it happens.

e4f58a3fdc.what_happened: A data entry officer at a private company has been arrested over an online banking fraud involving Rs. 1 million. The Wariyapola Computer Crime Investigation Division investigated after a person complained that Rs. 1 million had been taken from his bank account. The victim had been tricked into giving his bank account login details through a fraudulent website made to look like a private bank's official site.
details: A data entry officer at a private company has been arrested over an online banking fraud involving Rs. 1 million. The Wariyapola Computer Crime Investigation Division began investigating after a person complained that Rs. 1 million had been taken from his bank account.

The investigation found that the victim was tricked into giving his bank account login details through a fraudulent website. The fake site was designed to look like the official website of a private bank.

Using information from the investigation, officers arrested the suspect around noon yesterday (26). The suspect is 25 years old and lives in Ragama. The Wariyapola Computer Crime Investigation Division is conducting further investigations.

63523d7218.what_happened: Electricity and water shortages have become part of daily life in Ukraine's capital. Businesses are using generators when the power goes out. Al Jazeera's Audrey Macalpine shows how residents are adapting.
details: Electricity and water shortages have become part of daily life in Ukraine's capital, Al Jazeera reports. The shortages are happening while Ukraine is at war with Russia.
When the power goes out, businesses use generators to keep going. Al Jazeera's Audrey Macalpine shows how residents of the capital are adapting to these cuts.
key_facts: Electricity and water shortages are now part of daily life in Ukraine's capital.
Businesses use generators when the power goes out.
The shortages come amid Ukraine's war with Russia.
Al Jazeera's Audrey Macalpine shows how residents are adapting.
63523d7218.blurb: Power and water cuts are now daily life in Ukraine's capital, where businesses run generators and residents adapt.
63523d7218.spoken: Good evening. We're heading to Ukraine's capital, where life has changed because of the war with Russia. Electricity and water shortages are now just part of everyday life there. When the power goes out, businesses keep going by switching to generators. Al Jazeera's Audrey Macalpine has been seeing how residents are adapting to these daily cuts. It's a look at how ordinary people and shops cope when the lights and the water supply can't be relied on. That's the picture from the capital tonight, as Ukraine continues its war with Russia.
63523d7218.subject: Ukraine power crisis

303cde64eb.what_happened: Sri Lanka’s Department of Meteorology forecast heavy showers above 100 mm in parts of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Southern and Uva provinces on 27 November 2026. It also expected showers in the Northern, North-central and Eastern provinces and thundershowers elsewhere after 1.00 pm. The public was advised to take precautions against temporary localized strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.
details: The forecast was issued at 05.30 a.m. on 27 November 2026 by the Department of Meteorology. Misty conditions may prevail in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and Central provinces and in the Galle, Matara and Badulla districts during the early hours of the morning. Several spells of showers will occur in the Northern, North-central and Eastern provinces, while showers or thundershowers will occur at several places elsewhere in the island after 1.00 pm.

Heavy showers above 100 mm are likely at some places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Southern and Uva provinces. The general public is requested to take adequate precautions to minimize damage caused by temporary localized strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.

Showers or thundershowers may occur in sea areas off the coast extending from Mannar to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle, Matara and Hambantota. Showers or thundershowers will occur in several other sea areas around the island during the evening or night. Winds will be north-easterly or variable in direction, with speeds of 25-35 kmph.

Wind speeds may increase up to 40-45 kmph at times in sea areas off the coast extending from Kankesanthurai to Puttalam via Mannar and from Trincomalee to Matara via Batticaloa and Hambantota. These sea areas will be fairly rough at times, while other sea areas around the island will be moderate. Temporarily strong gusty winds and very rough seas can be expected during thundershowers.
303cde64eb.why_it_matters: The public is advised to take precautions to reduce damage from temporary localized strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.

Misty conditions may linger in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and Central provinces and in Galle, Matara and Badulla during the early hours. The public is asked to take precautions against temporary localized strong winds and lightning during thundershowers. At sea, showers or thundershowers are possible from Mannar to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle, Matara and Hambantota, and in other sea areas during the evening or night. Winds will be north-easterly or variable at 25 to 35 kilometres per hour, rising to 40 to 45 in some sea areas, where seas can be rough and very rough during thundershowers.

58d17d5d05.what_happened: Parliament observed a moment of silence today (27) for people who died or were injured in Cyclone Ditwah. Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne announced the commemoration in Parliament. It marked one year since Cyclone Ditwah battered Sri Lanka on November 27, 2025.
details: A moment of silence took place in Parliament today (27) for those who lost their lives and those injured because of Cyclone Ditwah. Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne made the announcement in Parliament. The Speaker said it was held to remember people affected by the natural disaster.
The event marked one year since Cyclone Ditwah battered Sri Lanka on November 27, 2025. Members of Parliament, along with the Speaker, stood up to observe a moment of silence for the victims.

Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne announced the commemoration, saying it was held to honor those who lost their lives and those who were injured when the cyclone battered Sri Lanka. 7dc393ee7f.what_happened: The Sri Lanka Navy caught seven suspects and seized a boat believed to be carrying heroin and crystal methamphetamine (ICE) in international waters south of Dondra. The search went beyond Sri Lanka's Exclusive Economic Zone. The stateless boat and the seven suspects are now being taken ashore.
details: The Sri Lanka Navy caught seven suspects and took control of a boat thought to be carrying heroin and crystal methamphetamine, also called ICE. This happened during a search in international waters south of Dondra, in an area past Sri Lanka's Exclusive Economic Zone. The boat had no nationality, so it was stateless.

The Navy said it ran the operation together with local and foreign intelligence agencies and maritime partners. The stateless boat and the seven suspects are now being escorted to shore. There they will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for more investigations and legal proceedings.

The Navy said closer coordination with regional and international maritime partners and stronger surveillance made the operation work. Its Information Fusion Centre in Colombo pulls together data from modern tools, including satellites, to judge intelligence and sea threats. Joint aerial surveillance with the Sri Lanka Air Force has widened how much ocean it can watch.

This seizure came under the government's 'A Nation United' anti-narcotics campaign, started in October 2025. Under that campaign, the Navy has seized drugs with an estimated street value above Rs. 116 billion. Since January 2026, it has handed over 66 boats, including four foreign vessels, and 379 suspects, including 18 foreign nationals, for legal proceedings over drug smuggling. The Navy said more details about the latest seizure will come later.
key_facts: Sri Lanka Navy caught seven suspects and seized a boat south of Dondra.
Boat suspected of carrying heroin and crystal methamphetamine (ICE); it was stateless.

Boat and suspects being taken ashore for the Police Narcotic Bureau.

7dc393ee7f.whats_next: The boat and seven suspects will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for investigation and legal proceedings, and the Navy will release more details later.

7dc393ee7f.spoken: Now here's a story from the waters off Sri Lanka. The country's Navy has caught seven people and taken charge of a boat they believe was packed with heroin and a powerful drug called crystal methamphetamine, or ICE. This happened far out at sea, south of a place called Dondra, in international waters beyond Sri Lanka's own zone. The Navy says it worked with intelligence teams from here and abroad to pull it off. The boat had no flag or nationality, and it's now being brought to shore, where the seven suspects will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for questioning and possible charges. The Navy says this is part of an anti-drug campaign launched in October 2025, which has already led to seizures worth over a hundred and sixteen billion rupees. 685a93c8bc.what_happened: Amnesty International renewed calls for accountability and an end to decades of impunity in Sri Lanka after a new United Nations report on attacks on humanitarian assistance during the country's internal armed conflict. The group's South Asia Director, Smriti Singh, said no progress has been made on crimes under international law, with truth, justice and reparations still out of reach for hundreds of thousands of victims.
details: Amnesty International renewed its calls for accountability and an end to decades-long impunity for conflict-related crimes in Sri Lanka. This came after a new report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) looking at attacks on humanitarian assistance during the internal armed conflict.

Amnesty's South Asia Director, Smriti Singh, said no progress had been made on crimes under international law, and that truth, justice and reparations remain elusive for hundreds of thousands of victims. She said the report showed successive Sri Lankan governments were unwilling to investigate allegations and ensure accountability for abuses committed during the conflict that ended in 2009.

Singh said impunity continues even as mass graves are still being identified, including in Chemmani, where recent exhumations uncovered the remains of more than 583 individuals, including children. She said attacks on humanitarian activities in Sri Lanka had become a model and precursor to similar incidents in conflicts around the world, and warned that impunity there could encourage crimes and undermine international law elsewhere.

Amnesty stressed the need for continued international scrutiny and urged UN member states to use the OHCHR Sri Lanka Accountability Project's resources, including through universal jurisdiction. The report, titled 'I Died Many Times: Attacks on Humanitarian Assistance in Sri Lanka, 20 Years On', examines attacks on humanitarian personnel and operations and the restriction and denial of aid by all parties in the conflict's final phase. The Accountability Project was set up under UN Human Rights Council Resolution 46/1 of 2021 to collect, consolidate, analyze and preserve evidence of serious violations, abuses and related crimes.
685a93c8bc.why_it_matters: Impunity in Sri Lanka could encourage crimes and undermine international law elsewhere, and attacks on humanitarian aid there became a model for similar incidents in conflicts worldwide.

685a93c8bc.spoken: Here's a story out of Sri Lanka. Amnesty International is again demanding accountability for crimes tied to the country's long internal armed conflict, which ended back in 2009. The push follows a new United Nations report, from the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, looking at attacks on humanitarian aid during that war. Amnesty's South Asia Director, Smriti Singh, says nothing has really changed. She points out that truth, justice and reparations are still out of reach for hundreds of thousands of victims, and that successive governments have been unwilling to investigate. She also mentions mass graves still being found, including in Chemmani, where more than 583 remains, some of them children, were recently uncovered. Amnesty is urging UN member states to use the accountability project's resources to push for justice.

249b0ed611.what_happened: Kenneth Law, a 61-year-old Canadian former chef who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries, apologised in court on Friday to the families of his victims. He spoke at a sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, where prosecutors asked for 25 years in prison and his defence lawyer asked for 12. He pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario and has admitted causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.
details: Kenneth Law, a 61-year-old former chef from Canada, sold toxic chemicals to people he met in online suicide forums, sending about 1,200 packages to recipients in 40 countries, with roughly a quarter of them going to the UK. On Friday he spoke at his sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, telling the families of victims that he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them. He said words can never replace the loss of their loved ones, offered his deepest condolences, and said he remains remorseful and sorry.

Law pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada. He has also admitted causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales. Under a plea deal, Canadian authorities withdrew more serious charges of murder, and he will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths.

At Friday's hearing, prosecutors asked the judge for a 25-year prison term and stressed that many victims were young and struggling with mental distress. Because he would get credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest, the recommended sentence would mean just under 20 years in prison. Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty called Law a predator who took advantage of vulnerable people, saying they needed help but found Law and his products for death, and she said his motive was financial: if people could pay, he sold to them, with no questions about their circumstances.

Defence lawyer Matthew Gourlay disagreed, arguing Law was not responsible for the victims' battles with mental illness, that each incident is its own unique tragedy, and that while Law may be a common denominator, he was not the cause of the hardships that made people seek his products; Gourlay said Law held a misguided belief that he was helping, and asked for a 12-year sentence. The hearing followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court about the pain Law caused. Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date, and the BBC pointed readers to its Action Line for organisations that offer information to anyone affected.

About 1,200 packages went to 40 countries; roughly a quarter were sent to the UK.

He admitted dozens of deaths in England and Wales; murder charges were withdrawn under a plea deal.
Under the plea deal he faces no UK charges over British deaths.
Prosecutors want 25 years, defence wants 12; time served since May 2023 arrest counts.
Doherty called him a predator; Gourlay said he had a misguided belief he helped.
Sentencing is due later, after September family impact statements are considered.
249b0ed611.whats_next: Sentencing is due at a later date, and the impact statements from grieving family members and friends given in September will be taken into account.

Law told the families he is sorry and remorseful. Sentencing comes at a later date, and statements from grieving families will be considered.

details: The source is a newswire. A man is suspected of killing a 45-year-old woman in the Mahailluppallama area of Eppawala. He was hospitalised after he hit a wild elephant while he was running away.

06798f5fb6.what_happened: Two Sri Lankan workers were killed after being struck by a cargo truck in South Korea. The accident happened while they were walking home along a road without pavement after finishing work at a nearby factory.
details: Two Sri Lankan workers in their 30s were killed in a road accident in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea. They were walking home after finishing work at a nearby factory when a cargo truck's protruding roof struck them.

The accident occurred at around 9.10 p.m. on November 26 on a road with no pavement, forcing pedestrians to walk along the roadside. A section of a wooden house roof was protruding from the passing cargo truck when it hit the workers, killing them both.

The truck driver told police he had failed to properly observe the road ahead. Investigations revealed he was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs at the time of the accident, and South Korean police have taken legal action against him while investigating whether cargo-loading regulations were violated. The identities of the deceased Sri Lankans have not yet been publicly disclosed.

Workers were walking home from a factory after their shift
A wooden house roof protruding from a cargo truck struck them

Police took legal action and are investigating cargo-loading rules
Identities of victims not yet publicly disclosed

06798f5fb6.spoken: A tragic accident in South Korea took the lives of two Sri Lankan workers walking home after their shift. The men, in their thirties, were struck by a cargo truck whose roof was protruding onto a road with no pavement in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi Province. The crash happened just before nine ten at night on November twenty-sixth. Police say the driver failed to see them ahead and was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Authorities have taken legal action and are now investigating whether cargo-loading regulations were violated. The workers' identities have not been publicly released, and investigations into the cause continue.

8d6cdbff6f.what_happened: A government-funded clinic in Sweden called Mottagning Neuropsykiatri offers free reassessments for ADHD and autism diagnoses, believed to be the first of its kind worldwide. People like Freya and Johanna seek reassessment because their diagnoses prevent them from joining the police or other professions. The clinic focuses on current symptoms rather than past history.
details: The clinic, Mottagning Neuropsykiatri, opened as ADHD and autism diagnosis rates rise globally. Some young adults, including Freya (not her real name) and Johanna, request reassessment because they no longer feel the diagnosis fits and it blocks career paths like policing. Freya was diagnosed at 12 but doubts it; Johanna was diagnosed at 14 and reassessed at 21 during a pilot, after which she no longer met criteria.

In Sweden, ADHD and autism historically barred people from military, police, train driver, and pilot roles. Since 2022, medication-free ADHD individuals can join the military; since 2021, those with ADHD or autism can apply to the police but must provide a medical certificate costing about 15,000 SEK (£1,100) privately. The clinic offers free reassessment, which can update medical records and ease job applications.

Medical consensus from WHO and UK bodies says autism is lifelong and ADHD persists into adulthood. Lead psychologist Sebastian Lundström says the clinic does not 'de-diagnose' but reassesses current functioning, adding a note to records rather than erasing the original diagnosis. He suggests some may have been misdiagnosed or a minority may outgrow symptoms. Critics like Navid Ghannad of Autism Skåne warn that removing diagnoses risks future support access if symptoms return, and could deepen stigma. Lundström says the risk is low, noting that during the pilot some who wanted to lose their diagnosis were told they still met criteria.
8d6cdbff6f.why_it_matters: The clinic highlights tension between medical consensus that ADHD and autism are lifelong and a system where diagnoses create employment barriers. Reassessments may help individuals access jobs but risk reinforcing stigma and leaving people without support if symptoms reappear.

Believed to be world's first clinic dedicated solely to reassessment.

Critics warn reassessments could deepen stigma and cut off future support access.

8d6cdbff6f.spoken: In Sweden, a unique government-funded clinic called Mottagning Neuropsykiatri is offering free reassessments for ADHD and autism diagnoses. It's believed to be the first clinic in the world dedicated only to this. People like Freya, who was diagnosed with ADHD as a child, are going there because having that diagnosis on their record stops them from becoming police officers. In Sweden, ADHD and autism used to bar you from jobs like the military, police, train driving, and piloting. The rules have relaxed a bit recently, but you still need an expensive medical certificate to apply for the police. The clinic checks how you're functioning right now, not just your history. If they decide you no longer meet the criteria, they add a note to your records. But experts warn that autism and ADHD are lifelong conditions. Removing the diagnosis could mean losing access to support later if symptoms come back, and it might make the diagnosis seem like something bad. The clinic says they're careful and don't remove diagnoses if people still need them.
8d6cdbff6f.subject: ADHD autism diagnosis reassessment
